THE IDEA

From task competence
to better execution.

Learning effective real-robot policies involves both acquiring basic task competence and improving execution efficiency. Evo-RL organizes these objectives into a staged data loop: teleoperated demonstrations initialize a vision-language-action policy, human interventions provide corrections in unfamiliar states, and selected autonomous experience supports further policy refinement.

A value model assesses experience to guide the selection of promising behavior for policy fine-tuning. The current study examines precision insertion, deformable manipulation, and multi-object packing. Alongside this workflow, RW-RL brings demonstrations, human-intervention episodes, and autonomous rollouts into a unified dataset with synchronized trajectories, controller provenance, and hierarchical semantic annotations.

THE LEARNING LOOP

Demonstrate. Correct. Refine.

02 / METHOD

Evo-RL integrates imitation learning and value-guided refinement into a staged workflow. Each policy update continues from the previous checkpoint.

  1. 1

    Demonstration initialization

    Fine-tune a pretrained π0.5 VLA policy on teleoperated demonstrations to establish basic task competence.

  2. 2

    Human-guided recovery

    Collect corrections in states the policy struggles with. Mix demonstrations with human-controlled segments from successful intervention episodes.

  3. 3

    Value-guided refinement

    Use a learned value model to select promising segments. Incorporate successful autonomous rollouts in later rounds to improve execution.

How experience is used

The policy takes camera images, robot proprioception, and a task instruction as input, and generates action chunks. The current experimental setup uses a separate, task-specific, vision-only value model.

The frame-level objective penalizes elapsed execution time and human takeovers. Estimated advantages give selected behavior additional weight in the policy training mixture. Human corrections remain supervised training data.

ON REAL ROBOTS

Three tasks. Different challenges.

03 / EXPERIMENTS

We study precision insertion on PiperX, garment folding on SO-101, and multi-object packing on SO-101. Each platform uses two arms, an external RGB camera, and two wrist cameras.

CURRENT MANUSCRIPT RESULTS

Measuring policy improvement.

04 / RESULTS

The current draft compares human-data efficiency and policy improvement across learning stages. Reported values below are transcribed from its experimental tables; missing entries remain blank.

Read the metrics

SR is the percentage of successful attempts, aggregated across units U₁–U₅ and trials. It is not whole-task completion rate. TP is completed units per hour of robot execution, including timed-out trials. Each trial has a five-minute limit.
